thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: eu-central-1 elevated 5xx rate for Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Alerts: authproxy-5xx > 10% across edge-nodes. Possible downstream auth provider failures. Paging oncall@sre.

incident-bot: Severity: SEV2. Customer impact: client API calls failing with 502/503. See graphs: https://grafana.internal/r/prod/eu-central1/5xx

sara: oncall here. joining. First check: are tokens failing at authproxy or upstream third-party auth provider? Jamal, can you pull authproxy logs for the last 10m?

jamal: grabbing logs now — running tail on the proxy aggregated stream:

```
$ kubectl logs -l app=auth-proxy -n prod --since=10m | grep "upstream error" | tail -n 50
ERROR upstream error 502 from auth-provider-eu1: "connection refused"
WARN retrying auth request uid=... attempt=2
ERROR upstream error 503 from auth-provider-eu1: "service unavailable"
```

jamal: looks like our proxy is getting 502/503 from the upstream auth provider (auth-provider-eu1). Latency also spiking ~800-1200ms for auth calls.

kai: I'm seeing matching spikes on token exchange graphs and our edge request traces show auth step is the bulk of the latency. Also seeing increased 5xx in Dedicated pools where we validate tokens synchronously.

maria: ops-runner / infra — any network flaps in eu-central1? NAT / egress issues? I checked VPC flow logs, no obvious drop. AWS status shows "degraded" in eu-central-1 for some managed services earlier but no full outage (link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/...)

ops-runner: confirmed, no internal ELB errors. This looks like a third-party auth provider degradation in the eu region. They reported an "egress routing" issue in their status page 7m ago.

sara: okay mitigation plan options:
- Route auth requests to a cross-region fallback auth endpoint (global-auth) for affected traffic.
- Enable local soft-fail for token verification on low-sensitivity routes (TEMP) to reduce 5xx for Hosted API while we failover.
- Increase retries with exponential backoff on authproxy for 503s (short-term).
- If needed, move Dedicated pool traffic for specific tenants off eu-central1 to other regions.

jamal: I can flip the authproxy routing to fallback to global-auth cluster. Will push canary config to 10% first. Command I plan to run:

```
kubectl apply -f authproxy-fallback-canary.yaml -n prod
# authproxy-fallback-canary.yaml sets AUTH_FALLBACK=global-auth, PERCENT=10
```

sara: do it. Add a redirect header for debugging. Watch 5xx rate.

deploy-bot: deploy started: authproxy-fallback-canary -> k8s/prod (10% rollout)

jamal: canary in. Initial traffic (10%) shows 5xx drop for those requests to ~1.2% from 12%. No major regressions.

kai: I'm also increasing the token cache TTL for hosted edge from 5s -> 60s to reduce verification frequency while we stabilize. Pushing change now (hotfix).

maria: NOTE: enabling soft-fail will increase risk of accepting expired/invalid tokens for certain non-critical endpoints. Product has been notified. @ops-runner we should target only anonymous/public endpoints.

ops-runner: acknowledged. I'll prepare a scoped routing rule to only apply soft-fail for /v1/public/* and keep auth strict for billing/management APIs.

sara: monitoring: graphs show aggregate 5xx across hosted API dropping from 11% -> 4% after canary and TTL change. Dedicated pools still at ~6-8% for some tenants.

jamal: I'll scale up token verification workers on the dedicated clusters (replica +2) to help clear the backlog of pending validations. Scaling now.

deploy-bot: scale job started for dedicated-auth-verifier (replicas 3 -> 5)

maria: I've opened a ticket with the third-party auth provider (support ref 34212). They acknowledged the issue and say "mitigation rolling out; expected resolution in 30-45m".

kai: can we route specific high-traffic tenants away from eu-central1 dedicated pools? We have config to mark tenant->regional preference. I can create a temporary placement override for the top 5 tenants hitting errors.

sara: yes do that for tenants with highest error-rate and who agreed to region-failover in their SLA. Keep product@redwood copied.

jamal: making the placement overrides now, will monitor sessions. Also enabling more aggressive retry/backoff in the proxy for 502-> 3 retries with jitter.

sara: timeline so far: 00:00 pager triggered; 00:02 identified upstream auth provider errors; 00:05 pushed 10% fallback; 00:12 saw 5xx drop for canary; 00:18 scaled dedicated verifiers + tenant failovers. Still monitoring.

maria: customer impact notice draft for status page:
"We are seeing elevated 5xx errors in eu-central-1 caused by a degraded third-party authentication provider. Mitigations (regional fallback, increased caching, targeted scaling) are in place and traffic is being routed to reduce errors. Some customers on Dedicated pools may see intermittent errors or increased latency while we complete failover. Next update in 30 minutes."

sara: LGTM. Publish with note that full resolution depends on third-party fix.

ops-runner: publishing now to status.redwood.com and emailing on-call account reps for affected customers.

maria: docs/ops: capturing mitigation steps and commands in the incident runbook. I'll create a follow-up postmortem ticket (SEV2) and assign owners: cause = third-party auth egress; mitigations = routing fallback + cache + scaling; action items = improve cross-region failover automation, add synthetic checks for upstream auth latency.

jamal: logs show authprovider errors subsiding slowly — 503 -> 200 for some endpoints. Provider reports partial mitigation in progress.

kai: re-evaluating whether to rollback soft-fail on public endpoints once 5xx under 1% for 15m. We'll aim to tighten back to default security posture.

sara: handoff to post-incident oncall: @maria you'll own the postmortem, @jamal follow up on automation, @kai follow up on cache TTL changes. I'll remain primary until next update. If 5xx spike returns escalate to SEV1.

maria: noted. Creating the postmortem ticket and linking this thread.

incident-bot: Incident update saved to incident tracker: INC-2026-0421-3765001234

sara: thanks team. Monitoring continues. If anyone sees a regression ping me directly. :thumbsup
